grades: 9 to 12 (high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool)
name: Youth Ocean Advocates
what_you_do: Teen volunteers teach visitors about marine life and ocean protection, join conservation projects like beach cleanups and community science, and get behind-the-scenes tours and about 20 hours of training.
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in grades 9 to 12 in a high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool program when they apply. Tides is the easiest level (any high school-aged person); Currents is the hands-on volunteer level.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. The page does not mention a cost.
duration: One school year or one summer; at least 8 activities of about 3 to 5 hours each; can stay until the summer after senior year
deadline_text: School Year 2026-27 Currents interest form is closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the Summer 2027 interest form (its general timeline says January; confirm with the Aquarium). Info sessions run over Zoom in March (summer) and September (school year).
how_to_apply: Attend a required online info session, then complete the application, then interview. Accepted teens do training before starting shifts. Questions: YOA@seattleaquarium.org.
notes: The page says its timeline is rough and may change. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'
